_what: NR4A3 fusion junctions recovered from DEPOSITED SEQUENCE RECORDS — the survey that lit-targets-aso-breakpoint-census.json names as missing.
_why: That census states in its own words: 'Not a survey of sequence databases. Everything above except the TCF12 deposit comes from papers; the deposit came from NCBI elink, and no comparable sweep of the other partners' deposits has been read into this file.' This is that sweep.
_cost: $0 — NCBI E-utilities on a free GitHub Actions runner (run 31890517984, 9m03s).
_how_the_exon_pair_is_derived: By matching each deposit's OWN nucleotide sequence against this repository's committed transcript models (aso-premrna-sequences.json), requiring 16 nt exact on EACH side of the seam. Never read off a title.
_what_this_is_not: NOT a prevalence measurement. Deposit counts are not tumour counts: what gets cloned and deposited is chosen, not sampled.
NOT a claim any junction is druggable.
NOT independent patients wherever several records share an originating group or patent family.
⭐_the_alias_finding: Three of the four TAF15 deposits are titled with RETIRED symbols — 'hTAFII68-CHN' (AF162670.1), 'RBP56/CHN' (AJ243810.1), 'TAF2N-TEC' (AJ245932.1). None contains the string 'NR4A3' or 'TAF15'. A sweep using current gene symbols would have returned none of them. The alias table is the instrument.

TFG_e7__NR4A3_e3.⭐ status: NEW TO THIS REPOSITORY — the census carried NO exon-resolved TFG breakpoint at all (TFG appears in that file only inside its search string).
TFG_e7__NR4A3_e3.⚠ evidence_grade: ONE primary GenBank mRNA (AY532911.1, 'TFG-NR4A3 fusion protein, partial cds') plus FOUR Korean patent sequences that agree on the identical seam. The patent records are one family from one group — they are CORROBORATION OF A SEQUENCE, NOT four independent patients. No PMID is attached to any of the five.
TFG_e7__NR4A3_e3.⛔ not_a_frequency: Nothing here says what fraction of TFG-rearranged EMC breaks at exon 7.

TAF15_e6__NR4A3_e3.status: CONFIRMED at sequence level — the census had this from papers (k=3/3); these are the underlying deposits.
TAF15_e6__NR4A3_e3.⛔ WHAT IT DOES NOT DO — READ THIS BEFORE: It does NOT bound the intron-2 fraction and must not be read as reassurance about the 3/3 pricing. ASCERTAINMENT: all three primary deposits are from 1999–2000. The intron-2 acceptor was not described until 2019 (PMID 31020999). Cloning of that era used primers anchored in NR4A3 EXON 3, which STRUCTURALLY CANNOT recover an intron-2 junction — so zero intron-2 deposits is the EXPECTED result whether or not the variant is common. The absence carries essentially no evidence. The census's named risk on the TAF15 arm stands unchanged.

EWSR1_e7__NR4A3_e2.status: CONFIRMED at sequence level — census had k=1/20 from papers; this is an independent deposited patient sequence.
EWSR1_e7__NR4A3_e2.⚠ anchor_note: The EWSR1 side of this 175 nt record contributes only ~40 nt, so the assignment rests on a shorter donor block than the others (still ≥16 nt exact, the module's floor).
EWSR1_e7__NR4A3_e2.bearing_on_the_3_unresolved_EWSR1_tumour: The census leaves 3 of 20 EWSR1 tumours unresolved and notes they are 'likely' type 2. This deposit confirms e7::e2 is a real recurrent junction in a DIFFERENT patient — it does NOT resolve those three, and 'likely' remains not a count.

TCF12_e5__NR4A3_e3.status: RE-FOUND INDEPENDENTLY — the known deposit, recovered blind by the sweep. Serves as the end-to-end positive control.

EWSR1_e10__NR4A3_intron2crypticExon__NR4.⭐ status: NEW TO THIS REPOSITORY — a third EWSR1 breakpoint, and the first anywhere here that does not join NR4A3 exon 3. New on BOTH sides: exon 10 is not a named EWSR1 donor, and the intron-2 cryptic acceptor had only ever been recorded here for TAF15.

EWSR1_e10__NR4A3_intron2crypticExon__NR4.cryptic_exon_placement: NR4A3 intron 2, offset 897..969 of a 2208 nt intron, flanked 5' AG and 3' GT; byte-identical to nr4a3-intron2-cryptic-exon.json
EWSR1_e10__NR4A3_intron2crypticExon__NR4.⛔ why_the_previous_sweep_missed_it: It did not miss the RECORD — it retrieved it and dropped the finding. The seam matcher tested three hard-coded acceptor sites, this transcript resumes at none of them, so seam_match came back empty and the record fell out of the reported set. discover_junction() in nr4a3_nuccore_sweep.py now finds junctions by maximal alignment instead, and re-derives this one from the deposit's sequence alone.
EWSR1_e10__NR4A3_intron2crypticExon__NR4.designs: aso-ewsr1-intron2-designs.json + nr4a3-fusion-junction-atlas-ewsr1intron2.json (5 tiled, 5/5 clear the parent exclusion; deep screens NOT yet run)
EWSR1_e10__NR4A3_intron2crypticExon__NR4.⛔ not_a_frequency: One deposit, one tumour, no denominator, no PMID. It does NOT resolve the three unresolved EWSR1 tumours in PMID 12378528 — different report, different group, no patient identifier linking them.
EWSR1_e10__NR4A3_intron2crypticExon__NR4.⚠ see: ⛔⛔ TYPE_NOMENCLATURE_IS_NOT_COHERENT_ACROSS_SOURCES (this file) — the record labels itself 'type 5 fusion' and that label disagrees with its own sequence.

⛔ a_defect_in_my_own_classifier: classify_material() graded LG067227.1 and LG067228.1 as PATIENT_MATERIAL. That is WRONG. They are Korean patent filings ('Compositions for Preventing or Treating a Tumor Disorder Comprising TFG-TEC Protein Mutant'); the grader matched the word 'Tumor' in a patent title and there is no tissue_type or cell_line field to contradict it. The two sibling records DI433544.1/DI438966.1 were graded ENGINEERED_CONSTRUCT only because their titles happen to contain the token 'Construct'. Fix: treat a DI/LG/PAT accession prefix as a patent record and never grade it patient material. Until fixed, do not read the material field on any patent-prefixed accession. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-15: classify_material() now checks PATENT_ACCESSION_PREFIX (DI/DJ/DL/DM/DD/DE/LG/LP/GM/HV/JA/JB/JC/JD/JE/PAT) FIRST and returns PATENT_SEQUENCE, so a patent filing can no longer be graded from an accident of title wording. Verified: LG067227.1 and DI433544.1 both grade PATENT_SEQUENCE; AF524261.1 and S81242.1 still grade PATIENT_MATERIAL.
what_this_changes: TFG gains its first exon-resolved breakpoint, so a TFG arm is designable in principle where before it was not.
Two existing census entries gain independent sequence-level support.
NOTHING about coverage percentages changes here — these are junction identities, not prevalences, and the partner denominators are untouched.

⛔⛔ TYPE_NOMENCLATURE_IS_NOT_COHERENT_ACR._the_conflict: GenBank AF524261.1's own CDS qualifier reads /note="type 5 fusion". In the Panagopoulos numbering this repository uses, type 5 is EWSR1 exon 13 -> NR4A3 exon 3. The junction derived from that deposit's nucleotides is EWSR1 exon 10 -> NR4A3 intron-2 cryptic exon -> NR4A3 exon 3. Those are not the same junction, so at least one of the two labels is wrong.
⛔⛔ TYPE_NOMENCLATURE_IS_NOT_COHERENT_ACR.⭐_which_half_is_sound: THE EXON ASSIGNMENT, NOT THE TYPE LABEL. The junction was derived from the deposit's own sequence against this repository's committed transcript models WITHOUT consulting the record's notes: the 5' block ends at spliced-EWSR1 offset 1114 == the cumulative END of exon 10; a 72-nt segment matching neither spliced transcript sits exactly inside NR4A3 intron 2 at offset 897, flanked AG...GT; the 3' block resumes at offset 697 == the cumulative START of exon 3. The derivation THEN agreed independently with the depositor's own exon annotations ('contains exons 7 through 10 of EWS', 'contains exons 2b and 3 of TEC'). Two independent readings agree on exon 10; only the type NUMBER is unsupported.
⛔⛔ TYPE_NOMENCLATURE_IS_NOT_COHERENT_ACR.⛔_consequence_for_anyone_mapping_types_3: DO NOT ASSUME THE TYPE SERIES IS COHERENT. A definition for type 3 or type 4 obtained by interpolating an assumed-consistent series may rest on a false premise, because here a source applies 'type 5' to a junction that is not this repository's type 5. Either the nomenclature differs between groups, or this record's label is an error — NOTHING IN THIS SWEEP RESOLVES WHICH, and it is recorded unresolved rather than argued away.
⛔⛔ TYPE_NOMENCLATURE_IS_NOT_COHERENT_ACR._rule_this_implies: Key every reagent and every coverage row on the SEQUENCE-DERIVED exon pair, never on a type label. A type label is a citation-provenance question, not a sequence one.
